Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) has fallen to its lowest price since August, trading at approximately $71,300 after the announcement of Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO of NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA). As of November 12, 2026, Bitcoin is down 3.9% in 24 hours. It hasn't traded this low since August 20, when it hit a daily low of $68,853.

However, Bitcoin had been in a downward trend for weeks before Huang's exit, down 14.2% over the past month. So, did NVIDIA's news drive Bitcoin lower, or did it hit an already struggling market?

NVIDIA Blog / Press
Bitcoin's Decline Started Before NVIDIA's CEO Change
Shutterstock

NVIDIA's release filed with the SEC says Huang "has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately." Chief financial officer Colette Kress will step in as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent replacement, with Harvey C. Jones becoming the board's first-ever chair.

Investors had a heads-up, as reports on November 11 indicated that the board was considering Huang's removal. After the news, NVIDIA's stock fell 6.4% in early trading and has dropped 18.8% over the past week.

Bitcoin's decline had already begun before Huang's resignation. It closed at $80,428 on November 4 and fell to $75,969 the following day. By November 10, Bitcoin had hit an intraday low of $72,643, already its lowest level since August at the time.

NVIDIA's Drop Spilled Into Bitcoin Because the Same Investors Own Both
gnepphoto / Shutterstock.com

Many Bitcoin investors also hold shares in AI companies like NVIDIA. Hedge funds, ETF buyers, and retail investors often have positions in both markets. When one asset drops, these investors tend to sell their other holdings to raise cash, and Bitcoin is particularly exposed because it trades around the clock.

Stock Futures Point to Lower Open

The major stock indexes appear likely to reverse some of yesterday's gains today. Futures tied to the Nasdaq 100 were about 1.2% lower, while those tied to the S&P 500 down 0.6%. Read our full coverage of today's markets here.

Nvidia Searching for CEO Candidates

Uncertainty about Nvidia (NVDA) leadership has pulled the company's shares down more than 8% this morning, influencing moves in assets beyond those of the chip giant. Nvidia's board convened late last night to consider ousting CEO Jensen Huang, who reportedly had extramarital affairs with a subordinate and a Chinese spy, Bloomberg reported. Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies worldwide, hired an external firm to identify potential CEO candidates, Bloomberg reported. Tesla and SpaceX chief Elon Musk said it "would be an honor" to hire the high-profile tech executive.

Tech Stocks Move as Nvidia Drama Unfolds

Nvidia's drama is weighing on segments of the stock market, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropping and stocks that the AI giant invested in tumbling. Shares of CoreWeave (CRWV) were recently down more than 10% after rising yesterday on earnings, while Coherent (COHR) and Lumentum Holdings (LITE) shares were off by roughly 6%. Nvidia competitor Advanced Micro Devices' (AMD) stock was recently ticking higher. Memory and data storage stocks, which have benefitted from Nvidia's rise, appeared to be generally falling, with the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) recently down more than 4%.

US stock futures traded mostly lower on Thursday, November 12, 2026, as reports concerning Nvidia's leadership and renewed uncertainty over semiconductor exports to China weighed on technology stocks.

At 03:09 ET (08:09 GMT), Nasdaq 100 futures declined 0.9%, or 240 points, while S&P 500 futures fell 0.4%, or 32 points. Dow Jones futures were broadly unchanged.

The declines followed gains on Wall Street on Wednesday, when the Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.6%, supported by renewed interest in artificial intelligence companies, including CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) and OpenAI (NASDAQ:OAI).

Markets also continued to assess higher-than-expected US inflation data, which had increased expectations of a larger Federal Reserve interest rate increase in December.

Nvidia Shares Fall Following Reports Concerning CEO

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) shares declined more than 6% in extended trading following a Wall Street Journal report that the company's board was considering the future of Chief Executive Jensen Huang.

The report cited allegations concerning Huang's personal relationships, including an alleged connection to an individual linked to Chinese intelligence. The allegations and any potential leadership change remained unconfirmed.

Huang, who owns approximately 3.6% of Nvidia, has played a central role in the company's expansion within the artificial intelligence semiconductor market.

Analysts at Yorkville Ives estimated that Nvidia could lose approximately 25% of its market valuation if Huang departed, although this remained a hypothetical assessment.

Alibaba Declines Amid Semiconductor Export Concerns

Alibaba (NYSE:BABA) shares fell more than 6% in Hong Kong trading amid concerns that developments involving Nvidia could lead to additional US scrutiny of semiconductor exports to China.

Reports linked Alibaba's access to Nvidia computing equipment through Megaspeed to individuals mentioned in the allegations surrounding Huang. These reported connections had not been independently established.

Other Chinese artificial intelligence companies, including MiniMax and Z.AI, also declined.

According to Bloomberg, Chinese authorities urged Washington not to use the allegations as grounds for additional chip export restrictions.

Investors were also awaiting quarterly results from Alibaba and Tencent, with attention focused on artificial intelligence investment and access to computing infrastructure.

Technology Earnings in Focus

Further technology-sector earnings were expected from Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) and Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) after the US market close.
